name: HCPL-3120-000E
title: 2.5 A output current IGBT gate drive optocoupler (HCPL-3120, HCPL-J312, HCNW3120)
summary: An isolated gate driver: an input LED lights a shielded detector IC whose totem-pole output sources and sinks up to 2.5 A peak into an IGBT or MOSFET gate from a 15 V to 30 V supply. The output stays low below an under-voltage lockout threshold with hysteresis, its low level is 0.5 V max, and propagation delay is 0.5 µs max with 25 kV/µs minimum common-mode rejection. HCPL-3120 (GaAsP LED), HCPL-J312 and HCNW3120 (AlGaAs LED) differ in package and insulation rating.

notes: #XXX options name older products; products launched since 15 July 2001 and RoHS-compliant options use -XXXE.

An order code is the part number joined to the option, e.g. HCPL-3120-560E: 300-mil DIP gull-wing surface mount, tape and reel, IEC/EN/DIN EN 60747-5-5 approval, RoHS compliant. HCPL-3120 alone is the 300-mil DIP in a tube, not RoHS compliant.

circuits.title: Recommended LED drive and application circuit
circuits.description: The optocoupler drives the high-side IGBT of one leg of a three-phase inverter, with no negative gate supply. On the input side a 270 Ω resistor from +5 V feeds the LED anode, and the cathode, pin 1 and pin 4 sit at input ground. The output of a 74XXX open-collector buffer is tied to the anode: when the buffer pulls low it shorts the anode to ground and holds the LED off; when it lets go, the resistor drives the LED on. The output side floats on the IGBT emitter: an 18 V supply from VEE (the emitter) to VCC, a 0.1 µF capacitor across pins 8 and 5, and pins 6 and 7 together through Rg to the gate. The off-state gate is held to the emitter through Rg and the DMOS pull-down.

parts.note: high side of one inverter leg; pins G, C, E
low side of the same leg; pins G, C, E

notes: The bridge has three legs, each two IGBTs with anti-parallel diodes; one optocoupler drives Q1, the high side of one leg.
With the LED shunted while off, this circuit reaches 25 kV/µs CMR.

circuits.title: HCPL-3120 typical application circuit with negative IGBT gate drive
circuits.description: The same input stage as the recommended circuit: 270 Ω from +5 V to the anode, the cathode and pins 1 and 4 at input ground, and an open-collector 74XXX buffer on the anode that shunts the LED off. On the output side two supplies are stacked on the IGBT emitter: VCC = 15 V above it to pin 8 and VEE = -5 V below it to pin 5, so the gate swings from +15 V to -5 V relative to the emitter. A 0.1 µF capacitor sits across pins 8 and 5, and pins 6 and 7 drive the gate through Rg.

circuits.title: Recommended LED drive circuit for ultra-high CMR
circuits.description: Input stage that shunts the LED while it is off. The anode and the collector of an NPN transistor go to +5 V; the transistor's emitter and the cathode share a node that a resistor returns to ground. With the transistor on, its collector-emitter path lies across the LED and keeps it off; with it off, current runs from +5 V through the LED and the resistor. Pins 1 and 4 are left open.

circuits.title: Not recommended open collector drive circuit
circuits.description: The LED anode goes to +5 V and the cathode through a resistor to the collector of an NPN transistor whose emitter is grounded; the transistor sinks the LED current to turn it on. In the off state nothing clamps the LED, so during a +dVcm/dt transient the current through the cathode-side coupling capacitance has to come through the LED; the drive is not recommended where very high CML is needed.

circuits.title: IOH test circuit
circuits.description: Measures the high-level output current. A 7 to 16 mA current source lights the LED. VCC is 15 to 30 V from pin 8 to pin 5 with a 0.1 µF bypass, pin 5 grounded. A 4 V source from VCC to the joined output pins holds VO 4 V below VCC while IOH is measured.

circuits.title: IOL test circuit
circuits.description: Measures the low-level output current. The LED pins are open, so the output is low. VCC is 15 to 30 V with a 0.1 µF bypass, and a 2.5 V source from pin 5 to the joined output pins holds VO 2.5 V above VEE while IOL is measured.

circuits.title: VOH test circuit
circuits.description: Measures the high-level output voltage. A 7 to 16 mA source lights the LED, VCC is 15 to 30 V with a 0.1 µF bypass, and a 100 mA current sink loads the joined output pins to pin 5; VOH is read at the output.

circuits.title: VOL test circuit
circuits.description: Measures the low-level output voltage. The LED pins are open, VCC is 15 to 30 V with a 0.1 µF bypass, and a 100 mA current source from VCC feeds the joined output pins; VOL is read at the output.

circuits.title: IFLH test circuit
circuits.description: Finds the input threshold current. A ramped current source drives the LED; VCC is 15 to 30 V with a 0.1 µF bypass. IFLH is the LED current at which VO rises past 5 V.

circuits.title: UVLO test circuit
circuits.description: Finds the under-voltage lockout thresholds. The LED carries 10 mA while VCC is ramped up and back down across a 0.1 µF bypass; the thresholds are the supply levels at which VO crosses 5 V.

circuits.title: tPLH, tPHL, tr and tf test circuit
circuits.description: Measures propagation delays and output edges. A 10 kHz, 50% duty-cycle pulse source drives the LED through 500 Ω for IF = 7 to 16 mA. VCC is 15 to 30 V with a 0.1 µF bypass, and the joined output pins drive 10 Ω in series with 10 nF to pin 5. Delays run from the LED current edges to the 50% point of VOUT; rise and fall times run between the 10% and 90% points.

circuits.title: CMR test circuit
circuits.description: Measures common-mode transient immunity. A 5 V source feeds a resistor to switch position A; the switch common goes to the anode, and position B goes to the input ground, which also holds the cathode and pins 1 and 4. Switch at A gives IF = 10 mA (output high, CMH); switch at B gives IF = 0 mA (output low, CML). The output side runs on VCC = 30 V with a 0.1 µF bypass. A 1500 V pulse generator between the input ground and pin 5 applies the common-mode edge while VO is watched.

operation.text: Three gate drive optocouplers share the specifications: the HCPL-3120 with a GaAsP LED, and the HCPL-J312 and HCNW3120 with an AlGaAs LED. Each LED shines onto a detector IC with a power output stage. HCPL-3120 and HCPL-J312 come in a 300-mil DIP-8, HCNW3120 in a 400-mil wide-body DIP-8, all with gull-wing surface-mount options. The HCNW3120 has the highest working insulation voltage, VIORM = 1414 VPEAK; the HCPL-J312 has 1230 VPEAK, and the HCPL-3120 630 VPEAK with option 060.

The output stage drives power IGBTs and MOSFETs directly, up to IGBTs rated 1200 V/100 A. Bigger IGBTs take a discrete power stage between the part and the gate. Applications listed: IGBT/MOSFET gate drive, AC and brushless DC motor drives, industrial inverters and switch mode power supplies.
A 0.1 µF capacitor is required between pin 8 (VCC) and pin 5 (VEE).

operation.topic: Low output voltage and no negative drive
operation.text: The pull-down is a DMOS transistor of about 1 Ω (typical), which gives VOL 0.5 V max. With the output low, the IGBT gate sees its emitter through Rg plus that 1 Ω. Keeping Rg small and the lead inductance to the IGBT gate and emitter short, for instance by mounting the part on a small board directly above the IGBT, can remove the need for a negative gate supply in many designs.

IGBT collector and emitter traces routed close to the input couple transients into it and degrade performance. Where the IGBT drain has to pass near the input, reverse-biasing the LED in the off state keeps coupled transients from turning the part on.

Step 1 sets the minimum Rg from the IOL peak rating, treating the IGBT gate and Rg as an RC load driven by the part; VOL at 2.5 A is taken as 2 V, a conservative figure. At small Rg the output is not an ideal voltage step, so the real peak current is lower than this predicts. Step 2 checks the part's dissipation and raises Rg if it is too high. In the worked example (negative gate drive circuit, IF worst case 16 mA, Rg = 8 Ω, duty cycle 80% max, Qg = 500 nC, f = 20 kHz, TA max 85°C): PE = 16 mA × 1.8 V × 0.8 = 23 mW; PO = 4.25 mA × 20 V + 5.2 µJ × 20 kHz = 85 mW + 104 mW = 189 mW, above the 178 mW PO(MAX) at 85°C (250 mW less 15°C × 4.8 mW/°C). The 4.25 mA is the 5 mA ICC maximum, which falls at –40°C, derated to 85°C along the ICC vs. temperature curve. The switching budget is 178 mW – 85 mW = 93 mW, so ESW(MAX) = 4.65 µJ, which the energy graph gives at Rg = 10.3 Ω for Qg = 500 nC.

In steady state all heat leaves through θCA and raises the case temperature TC. θCA depends on the board and is the designer's to find; 83 °C/W was measured with one part soldered in the middle of a 2.5 × 2.5 inch board with small traces, no ground plane, in still air, and the absolute maximum dissipation derating assumes that value. Example: with θCA = 83 °C/W, TA = 70 °C, an LED power of 0.045 W and an output power of 0.25 W, TJE = 70°C + 0.045 W × 339°C/W + 0.25 W × 140°C/W, about 120°C, and TJD = 70°C + 0.045 W × 140°C/W + 0.25 W × 194°C/W, about 125°C. Both junctions are to be kept at or below 125°C for the board layout and placement in use.

In an unshielded optocoupler, CMR failures come mainly from capacitance between the input side and the detector IC. In this part the detector carries an optically transparent Faraday shield that carries that coupled current away from the sensitive circuitry. The capacitance from the LED to output pins 5 to 8 remains (CLEDP from the anode, CLEDN from the cathode); during common-mode transients it disturbs the LED current and becomes the main cause of CMR failure. A high-CMR LED drive therefore has to hold the LED firmly on or off through the transient. The recommended application circuit reaches 25 kV/µs using few parts.
Driving the LED well above threshold keeps a transient from pulling its current below threshold. An LED current of at least 10 mA leaves enough margin over the 5 mA maximum IFLH for 25 kV/µs CMR.

The LED must stay at VF ≤ VF(OFF) through the transient. In the recommended circuit, during a –dVcm/dt edge the current in CLEDP also flows through the logic gate's RSAT and VSAT; as long as the gate's low-state voltage stays below VF(OFF), the LED stays off. An open-collector drive cannot hold the LED off on a +dVcm/dt edge, because all the current in CLEDN must then pass through the LED. Shunting the LED in the off state, as both the recommended application circuit and the ultra-high CMR drive circuit do, gives ultra-high CMR.

UVLO protects the IGBT when the supply (equal to the fully charged gate voltage) drops below what the IGBT needs to stay fully on with low resistance. With the output high, VCC falling below VUVLO– (9.5 V to 12.0 V) sends the output low after a typical 0.6 µs. With the output low and the LED on, VCC rising above VUVLO+ (11.0 V to 13.5 V) sends the output high after a typical 0.8 µs. On the UVLO graph the output switches at (12.3 V, 10.8 V) rising and (10.7 V, 9.2 V) falling.

Dead time is the interval when both the high-side and low-side transistors of a leg are off; any overlap in their conduction drives large currents through the power devices between the motor rails. PDD is specified to help keep dead time small. Delaying LED2's turn-on after LED1's turn-off by PDDMAX (350 ns over –40°C to +100°C) makes the worst-case minimum dead time zero: Q1 has just turned off as Q2 turns on. The maximum dead time is PDDMAX – PDDMIN = 350 ns – (–350 ns) = 700 ns over the same range. The delays are taken at one temperature and set of test conditions, since parts in one inverter sit close together and switch identical IGBTs.

The top of the DIP carries the device part number, a test rating code, date code (YYWW), lot ID, a special program code and the UL logo, with a pin 1 dot. A marking letter shows the option: "V" is option 060; options 300 and 500 are not marked.
